title: The Colour out of Space by H. P. Lovecraft

evidence.paraphrase: A five-acre expanse of grey desolation where nothing grows exists as a permanent alteration to the landscape.
evidence.quote: no other name could fit such thing, or any other thing fit such a name. It was as if the poet had coined the phrase from having seen this one particular region. It must, I thought as I viewed it, be the outcome of a fire; but why had nothing new ever grown over those five acres of grey desolation that sprawled open to the sky like a great spot eaten by acid in the woods and fields?

evidence.paraphrase: A meteorite arrives from the sky and embeds itself on the farm, introducing an object of extraterrestrial origin.
evidence.quote: the great rock that fell out of the sky and bedded itself in the ground beside the well at the Nahum Gardner place

evidence.paraphrase: University professors examine the meteorite and take a specimen to the college for testing.
evidence.quote: The professors tried it with a geologist's hammer and found it was oddly soft. It was, in truth, so soft as to be almost plastic; and they gouged rather than chipped a specimen to take back to the college for testing.

evidence.paraphrase: Spectroscopic testing reveals bands unlike any known spectrum, prompting talk of new elements and bizarre optical properties.
evidence.quote: when upon heating before the spectroscope it displayed shining bands unlike any known colours of the normal spectrum there was much breathless talk of new elements, bizarre optical properties, and other things which puzzled men of science are wont to say when faced by the unknown

evidence.paraphrase: Scientists systematically test the meteorite with a series of reagents and acids, none of which affect it.
evidence.quote: Hot as it was, they tested it in a crucible with all the proper reagents. Water did nothing. Hydrochloric acid was the same. Nitric acid and even aqua regia merely hissed and spattered against its torrid invulnerability.

evidence.paraphrase: The scientists conclude the substance is not of earth and follows laws foreign to earthly physics.
evidence.quote: It was nothing of this earth, but a piece of the great outside; and as such dowered with outside properties and obedient to outside laws.

evidence.paraphrase: The meteorite's magnetic and electrical properties are said to have repeatedly drawn lightning to the yard.
evidence.quote: The stone, magnetic as it had been, must have had some peculiar electrical property; for it had "drawn the lightning," as Nahum said, with a singular persistence. Six times within an hour the farmer saw the lightning strike the furrow in the front yard

evidence.paraphrase: The fruit and crops grow large but become inedibly bitter, and the entire harvest is ruined.
evidence.quote: Into the fine flavour of the pears and apples had crept a stealthy bitterness and sickishness, so that even the smallest of bites induced a lasting disgust. It was the same with the melons and tomatoes, and Nahum sadly saw that his entire crop was lost.

evidence.paraphrase: The vegetation develops strange colors and bizarre growth unrelated to the region's normal flora.
evidence.quote: All the orchard trees blossomed forth in strange colours, and through the stony soil of the yard and adjacent pasturage there sprang up a bizarre growth which only a botanist could connect with the proper flora of the region.

evidence.paraphrase: All the vegetation begins to glow faintly, and a piece of phosphorescence seems to move on its own.
evidence.quote: A dim though distinct luminosity seemed to inhere in all the vegetation, grass, leaves, and blossoms alike, while at one moment a detached piece of the phosphorescence appeared to stir furtively in the yard near the barn.

evidence.paraphrase: Mrs. Gardner goes mad, raving about indescribable things in the air.
evidence.quote: the poor woman screamed about things in the air which she could not describe. In her raving there was not a single specific noun, but only verbs and pronouns.

evidence.paraphrase: Livestock sicken, turning grey and brittle and disintegrating before death.
evidence.quote: The swine began growing grey and brittle and falling to pieces before they died, and their eyes and muzzles developed singular alterations.

evidence.paraphrase: Laboratory analysis links the dust samples to the meteor via matching spectroscopic bands that later fade.
evidence.quote: Under the spectroscope both samples gave off an unknown spectrum, in which many of the baffling bands were precisely like those which the strange meteor had yielded in the previous year. The property of emitting this spectrum vanished in a month, the dust thereafter consisting mainly of alkaline phosphates and carbonates.

evidence.paraphrase: Nahum, dying and disintegrating, manages a final answer to Ammi.
evidence.quote: the cleft, bulging lips were just able to crackle out a final answer.

evidence.paraphrase: Ammi explains the entity grew from the globule in the meteor and appears as a life-draining cloud of colour.
evidence.quote: it must be some'at growed from a round ball like one we all seen in the meteor stone that fell a year ago June. Sucks an' burns, he said, an' is jest a cloud of colour like that light out thar now

evidence.paraphrase: The farm erupts in a cataclysm of unnatural sparks and coloured fragments after the colour departs.
evidence.quote: there burst up from that doomed and accursed farm a gleamingly eruptive cataclysm of unnatural sparks and substance; blurring the glance of the few who saw it, and sending forth to the zenith a bombarding cloudburst of such coloured and fantastic fragments as our universe must needs disown

evidence.paraphrase: The colour entity shoots up into the sky and departs through the clouds toward space.
evidence.quote: Then without warning the hideous thing shot vertically up toward the sky like a rocket or meteor, leaving behind no trail and disappearing through a round and curiously regular hole in the clouds before any man could gasp or cry out.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator contrasts the entity with known matter, noting it obeyed laws outside our cosmos.
evidence.quote: In terms of matter I suppose the thing Ammi described would be called a gas, but this gas obeyed laws that are not of our cosmos.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator frames the phenomenon as a colour from outside all known Nature.
evidence.quote: It was just a colour out of space\u2014a frightful messenger from unformed realms of infinity beyond all Nature as we know it

evidence.paraphrase: The blight is said to continue spreading outward at roughly an inch per year.
evidence.quote: Botanists, too, ought to study the stunted flora on the borders of that spot, for they might shed light on the country notion that the blight is spreading\u2014little by little, perhaps an inch a year.
